Update from infra — preliminary root cause and immediate mitigations:

Root cause hypothesis:
- The pool's autoscaling policy is mis-evaluating incoming RPS distribution due to an edge case in the steady-state estimator; short, high-concurrency bursts are being treated as transient, so the autoscaler is under-provisioning GPU capacity and queue depth climbs.
- We also see KV-cache pressure (high eviction rate) which increases per-request token work. Combined, this produces queueing/backpressure and a rise in 5xx from admission timeouts.

Immediate actions taken (already in progress):
1) Enabled admission-control on fintranx-prod-dedicated to shed non-critical background requests and protect foreground traffic.
2) Temporarily widened the autoscaler sensitivity window for this pool (10 -> 30s) and bumped headroom by +20% to force a scale-up.
3) Initiated cross-pool overflow to us-west compatible nodes (controlled, with routing tag) — this will add capacity within ~3–6 minutes if no placement constraints.
4) Dropped non-essential batching to reduce KV pressure and pulled a small cached-shard into memory to reduce hits.

Risk and ask:
- The scaling policy change is safe but will increase cost if the burst persists. We recommend approving an emergency burst credit (2 weeks) and allowing the overflow to remain until traffic stabilizes.
- If overflow capacity is insufficient, we need authorization to provision two extra GPUs into the dedicated pool (estimated 48–72 hour lead for bare metal in our dedicated fleet).

I will continue to stream logs to the war-room and post an incident summary when we have stable p95 < 250ms and error rate returning to baseline.

Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Infra & Serving Runtime
